title: No partiality (Acts 10:34–48)
hookLine: Peter opens his mouth in a stranger's house and admits he's just learned something
tomorrow: who gave the believers their name? Acts leaves a blank.

cards: I see it now. I didn't before. Sentences like that only come after you've been wrong for a while.
Peter is standing in a Gentile's house in Caesarea. The room is full of Cornelius' relatives and close friends, all of them waiting to hear him.
He opens his mouth, and the first thing he says is something he has only just learned: "Of a truth I perceive that God is no respecter of persons." I perceive. Not, I have always known.
He says it as a discovery, made somewhere between a rooftop in Joppa and this doorway. Then he starts to preach, and partway through, something interrupts him.

teach.b: Respecter of persons is older English for someone who plays favorites, who judges by face, rank or nation.
Peter goes on: "But in every nation he that feareth him, and worketh righteousness, is accepted with him." Every nation.

Then he tells the story of Jesus of Nazareth, short and plain: a man "who went about doing good, and healing all that were oppressed of the devil," the cross, the third day, witnesses who ate and drank with him after he rose.
And then the interruption. "While Peter yet spake these words, the Holy Ghost fell on all them which heard the word."
The sermon isn't finished. The Spirit doesn't wait for it to be. That's the detail to tell a friend tonight: in this story, God doesn't let the preacher get to the end.
The believers who came with Peter are astonished, "because that on the Gentiles also was poured out the gift of the Holy Ghost."
And Peter asks: "Can any man forbid water, that these should not be baptized, which have received the Holy Ghost as well as we?"
On the desert road, the traveler from Ethiopia asked almost the same question: what doth hinder me? Here Peter answers it for a whole household.
They're baptized, and the scene ends with an invitation: they ask him to stay a few days.

how: Some Christians come back to Peter's words, God is no respecter of persons, when they talk about welcoming people of every nation and background.

o: a judge's duty to rule without bias in court
staying neutral in an argument between friends

s: Peter says he had always known God plays no favorites
he says, I perceive: a discovery, made after the rooftop vision.
the Spirit fell before Peter finished speaking
while Peter yet spake these words, the Holy Ghost fell on all them which heard.
Cornelius' household was baptized first, then received the Spirit
here it's the other way round: the Spirit fell, then Peter asked, can any man forbid water?

games.q: your team captain gives the best drills to her friends, and you're one of her friends. what does Peter's discovery ask of you?
o: say something, even though the favoritism helps you.
enjoy it; favorites are only wrong when you're left out.
wait until someone who's left out complains first.
games.why: God is no respecter of persons, in every nation. Peter learned it in a house where he was the insider, and changed how he acted there.

practice: Take a pen and paper and write three names: someone you admire, someone you barely notice, someone you find hard. Under each name, write the same short good wish, word for word.
Then sit with the page, and look at the three names side by side.

wordCard.voice: No partiality. Peter's discovery in Cornelius' house: God is no respecter of persons.

orig.note: Greek: respecter of persons, one who shows partiality; Acts 10:34.

carryVoice: Hold onto this: no respecter of persons, a thing Peter perceived, not a thing he'd always known. See you tomorrow.
